Internal helper: the "seems categorical" warning of jlm() and jlogistic()

Source: R/checks.R
dot-jst_seems_categorical_msg.Rd

A predictor that looks categorical and entered the model as a number gets a warning with the two ways to treat it as categorical, each as lines to run: register it with jdummy() and run the model again, or name it in categorical = for this call.

Usage

.jst_seems_categorical_msg(
  fn,
  v,
  formula,
  data_name,
  data_kind,
  default_used,
  categorical = NULL
)

Arguments

fn

Character(1); "jlm" or "jlogistic".

v

Character; the predictor's name, or the names of several.

formula

The formula as the call gave it.

data_name

Character(1); the data frame as the call named it, or the juse() default's name.

data_kind

What the call gave as its data, as .jst_data_arg_kind() reads it.

default_used

Logical; the call gave no data.

categorical

The call's own categorical =, kept in the second route's line.

Value

Character(1); the warning's text.

Details

Until Session 346 the rerun lines were built from .jst_unbacktick(deparse(formula)) on the REWRITTEN formula. deparse() returns one string for each 60 characters, so any longer formula printed cut off, with a stray closing parenthesis; the backticks a name such as `W2-W24 (binary)` needs were stripped with those of the computed terms; a variable already registered with jdummy() appeared as its dummy columns; and a call that named its data frame was offered jlm(y ~ x), which runs only with a juse() default (the S345 item). The lines are now built from the formula as typed, in one piece, with the data the call named. The second call sits on a line of its own: after "Or: " it was wrapped as prose, and a break could land inside a backticked name.

An expression given as the data (jlm(y ~ g, mk())) cannot be registered on, so the first route names it first (mydata <- mk()), as jrecode()'s reminder does since v0.9.217. Arguments of the call other than the formula and the data are not repeated.

Several predictors that seem categorical get ONE warning (Session 347): each had a warning of its own, with its own jdummy() line and the same refit line repeated. Now the names are joined in the first line, one jdummy() call takes them all, and categorical = lists them.
